title: Masks: where things may happen
summary: Make a mask of your own, paint it, build it from layers and rules, and see where it is used.

steps.title: Masks
steps.text: A mask is a picture of the map that says where something may happen: where rivers go, where forests grow, what to erode. Height layers, strata and prop rules read masks. Ten steps.

steps.title: The mask brush
steps.text: The mask brush paints the chosen mask. It is the one tool of the mode.

steps.title: The list of masks
steps.text: Each mask has a small picture that follows your strokes, and its size. Choose one to paint it and to edit it in the inspector. Under the list: a name field, Add a mask, Rename, Duplicate, Delete, and Show it over the terrain.

steps.title: Try it: add a mask
steps.text: Type a name if you like, then click Add a mask. A mask starts empty. Half the map's size makes a coarser mask, which is enough for most uses.
steps.done: The new mask is in the list and chosen. Delete removes it again, and so does undo.

steps.title: The brush's settings
steps.text: The chosen mask's name, the brush shape and how its edge fades, the radius and the strength, and Erase, which takes the mask away instead of adding it.

steps.title: Try it: paint a mask
steps.text: Press the left mouse in the top view and drag over the map. The painted part shows in colour over the terrain. Each stroke is one step of undo. A mask has to be chosen in the list first; add one if the list is empty.
steps.done: The painted part shows in colour. Ctrl+Z takes the stroke back.

steps.title: Seeing the mask
steps.text: Show it over the terrain keeps the chosen mask visible, also when another tool is active. The chip Mask above the views does the same.

steps.title: A mask is a stack of layers
steps.text: The inspector lists the layers of the chosen mask. A layer can be painted, an image, another mask, a stratum's mask, or rules. Each has a way of combining with the layers below, a strength and a clip. Up, Down and Remove arrange them. A rules layer builds a mask without painting: it follows the terrain by slope, height, distance from the water or noise, so grass on flat ground needs no brush.

steps.title: Where masks are used
steps.text: A height layer takes a mask as its clip, so it works only there. A stratum's layer can read a mask, and props can be placed by rules from one. Masks are for your tools: the game never gets them.

steps.title: That is the Masks mode
steps.text: Next: the Paint mode, where strata give the terrain its textures. Help, Tours lists it.
